Questions.Question: How many players can a club put on its main squad list?
How many places in the main squad list are reserved for locally trained players, and how many of those can be association-trained?
Questions.Answer: According to the UEFA Champions League regulations, eight places in the main squad list (List A) are reserved exclusively for locally trained players (Paragraph 31.04). Out of these eight spots, no club may have more than four association-trained players listed (Paragraph 31.04).

How many substitutions is a team allowed during a match?
Questions.Answer: A team is allowed to make up to five substitutions during a match, using a maximum of three stoppages in play to do so. Additionally, a sixth substitution can be made exclusively during extra time in knockout matches, and this does not reduce the number of stoppages in play available. Substitutions made before the start of the match, during half-time, between the end of normal playing time and extra time, and at half-time during extra time do not count against the three stoppages in play permitted during regular time or the additional stoppage in extra time.

Two clubs finish the league phase on the same number of points. How is the higher position decided?
Questions.Answer: If two or more teams are equal on points at the completion of the league phase, the following criteria are applied, in this order, to determine their rankings: 1) Superior goal difference in the league phase, 2) Higher number of goals scored in the league phase, 3) Higher number of away goals scored in the league phase, 4) Higher number of wins in the league phase, 5) Higher number of away wins in the league phase, 6) Higher number of points obtained collectively by league phase opponents, 7) Superior collective goal difference of league phase opponents, 8) Higher number of goals scored collectively by league phase opponents, 9) Lower disciplinary points total (based on yellow and red cards received), and 10) Higher club coefficient.

Questions.Question: A player is sent off in the last league phase match. Does that suspension carry into the knockout rounds?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a suspension resulting from a red card received in the last league phase match carries over into the knockout rounds. According to Paragraph 63.02(b), players and team officials are suspended for the next competition match after receiving a red card. This suspension applies to all subsequent matches within the same competition, including the knockout rounds.

Questions.Question: A club's first-choice goalkeeper is injured for two months. Can they bring in a replacement, and does the replacement have to be locally trained?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a club can temporarily replace their first-choice goalkeeper if the injury is considered long-term (lasting at least 30 days). The replacement goalkeeper does not have to be locally trained, even if the injured goalkeeper was locally trained, as stated in paragraph [31.14(aa)].

Questions.Question: After a defeat, is the head coach personally required to speak to broadcasters, and how quickly must the press conference start?
Questions.Answer: Yes, after a defeat, the head coach is required to speak to broadcasters and participate in the post-match press conference. The post-match press conference at the stadium must start no later than 20 minutes after the final whistle, as per Paragraph [80.02]. Additionally, the head coach is required to be available for various obligatory interviews, including at least five with audiovisual rights-holders immediately after the match, according to Paragraph [80.01(ee)].

Questions.Question: Can a club choose which ball is used for its home fixtures?
Questions.Answer: No, a club cannot independently choose which ball is used for its home fixtures. According to paragraph [50.01], match balls for the qualifying phase must comply with both the IFAB Laws of the Game and UEFA Equipment Regulations. Home clubs are required to provide visiting teams with the same match balls for training and warm-ups as those used during the match, thereby standardizing the match balls used.

Questions.Question: Does Liverpool's registered squad satisfy the locally trained player requirement?
Manchester United are short on club-trained players. How many can they actually register on List A as things stand?
Questions.Answer: As per regulation [31.04], Manchester United must have at least 8 locally trained players (consisting of either club-trained or association-trained players) to register the maximum of 25 players on List A. Currently, they have 3 club-trained players and 5 association-trained players, fulfilling the minimum requirement of 8 locally trained players. Therefore, Manchester United can register the full 25 players on List A.

Questions.Question: Real Madrid have registered the goalkeepers shown in their squad. Are they compliant on that front?
Questions.Answer: Yes, Real Madrid are compliant regarding their goalkeeper registrations. Based on the squad data, Real Madrid have registered two goalkeepers (Thibaut Courtois and Andriy Lunin). Regulation [41.02] requires the position of goalkeeper to use the number 1 if assigned, but it does not impose restrictions on the number of goalkeepers explicitly registered, as long as other squad rules are followed.
